title: House where police shooting occurred was home for homeless
subtitle: Former owner offered a roof for those with nowhere else to go, and willed the Third Street property to the Town of Collingwood, Home Horizon and Habitat for Humanity after she died in 2019
article: When Collingwood resident Gloria Culbert died in June of 2019, she hoped leaving her home to three local beneficiaries might mean her personal passion project might be able to continue.

Her former residence, at 167 Third Street, is currently part of an investigation by the province's Special Investigations Unit as the location of the shooting death of Matthew Rice by an OPP officer on Sept. 9. Prior to and since her death last year, Culbert had opened her home to people in the community experiencing homelessness who had nowhere else to go.
Upon her death, Culbert left her home to three beneficiaries in her will: the Town of Collingwood, Home Horizon and Habitat for Humanity South Georgian Bay.

"Gloria had a big heart when it came to serving the homeless, and I think all three beneficiaries are in agreement that it would be nice to do something that serves in her memory," said Garth Martin, chair of Home Horizon's board of directors.

"What I think she was aiming to do through her will was to ensure the house would be used in the same way, to support homelessness," he said. "I think she saw this as her own personal charity, where she was helping out vulnerable individuals who would otherwise be homeless by allowing them to live in her house. It's not clear how many people routinely paid rent, but they were asked to support the needs of the house."
Martin said the house was in a sad state of repair when Culbert died, which has lead to challenges when figuring out how to proceed with the property over the past year.

"My understanding of the designation of the three beneficiaries was that Habitat for Humanity might be in a position to do work on renovations to bring it up to standard, and since Home Horizon was in the business of serving the homeless, we could support the continuation of the house being used to serve the homeless," said Martin. "I'm not sure what she had in mind for the town, but if it were a town resource, they might be in a position to make all this happen in some co-ordinated fashion."
Martin said the challenge the beneficiaries are currently facing with the property is the cost of bringing the home up to standard.

"It's not really practical for any of the beneficiaries to figure out how to get the funds to bring the building up to a level to allow us to use it for the purposes she intended," he said, adding that now the beneficiaries are focused on finding reasonable alternatives that could also pay tribute to Culbert's memory.

Don McKay, Culbert's attorney and executor of her will, said the beneficiaries had a meeting this week to further discuss plans for the property, which was confirmed by Sara Almas, clerk for the Town of Collingwood.
"Things are still up in the air... around who is going to be the trustee for the property," said McKay.

McKay said Dwayne O'Connor, former executive director of Home Horizon, was very close with Culbert and as far as he knew has been dealing with the current tenants, who were paying what they could afford for bills associated with the property.

"We had been concerned due to the state of the building and a lack of any kind of supervision. There has been a sense of urgency in that there are people living there. It has not been ideal, by any means," said Martin, clarifying that Home Horizon has had no official involvement with the house aside from being named as a beneficiary, including the collecting of rent or home maintenance.
"Dwayne had, on his own, assumed some role in assisting with issues that were arising," said Martin.
O'Connor did not return a request for comment by publication time.
The province's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) is investigating the circumstances surrounding the shooting death of Matthew Rice, 29, on Sept. 9 outside the Third Street residence.

Preliminary information released by the SIU suggests that OPP officers attended the residence for a report of a barricaded man, and as officers were setting up the perimeter, the man exited the residence in possession of a firearm. The man was shot by an officer and was transported to hospital where he was pronounced deceased.
